Path written: `/home/dan/ForClaude/AzureDevOpsForager/AzureDevOpsForager.Server/wwwroot/vector-engines.html` I wrote it from scratch and reused no text from the earlier draft. I edited no other file and made no commit. The page is untracked in git, and nothing links to it yet: `writeups.html`, `index.html` and `sitemap.xml` all still miss it. **What came out of the data (and changed the "why" section)** - **Pass order skews p50.** Three engines ran the same query at two points in a run, and the later timing was always faster: - sqlite-vec: 2.16 ms first, 1.95 ms when timed last. - Qdrant with exact=true: 2.30 ms as its own target, 0.87 ms at the end of the next target. - SQL Server exact scan: 6.18 to 6.81 ms as the first target, 4.28 to 4.77 ms inside the DiskANN target. - Elasticsearch and OpenSearch averaged about half their p50 in the 1-searcher pass that followed. - The page says this, tags it measured, and the ranking uses the 8-searcher pass. - **SQL Server DiskANN vs exact.** The paired +1.5% to +16.4% (8 searchers) and +14.7% to +18.4% (1 searcher) are shown. The cause is tagged "likely run order", because exact always ran first and the exact query timed inside the DiskANN target matched DiskANN's p50. - **Qdrant built no HNSW graph.** Every load reports `indexNote` "0 of 524 vectors in HNSW segments", so both Qdrant rows are scans. The page says so. - **MongoDB also missed recall in run 3** (0.965, nDCG 0.535). It is listed with ClickHouse and DiskANN as the third exception. - **Not waited for.** The harness never calls Milvus `WaitForIndexAsync` or Oracle `RefreshIndexAsync`. The page discloses this as unchecked. - **Gains above 8x, every run:** only Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Milvus, MongoDB and MariaDB. The table's Gain column is the median of per-run ratios, not a ratio of medians. - **Wire format:** Typesense sits with ClickHouse and Weaviate as "vector written as text in a query". SQL Server sends JSON text in a TDS parameter. Exact mode bounds the JSON/HTTP cost at 2.22 ms (Vespa) and 4.29 to 4.41 ms (OpenSearch, Elasticsearch). **Checks run** - No em or en dashes, no banned words. - Sentences average 10.9 words. The longest is the 25-word default line in Reproduce. - Tags balance and all anchors resolve. - Every number in `
` either matches a consolidated or raw value or is a version, setting or date. - The dataset facts are not in `bench-results`. holes: Wrong number, 'Low gains' Redis bullet (line 240): '2.6 to 3.9 times'. Run 3 (20261004-132735) gives 3154.1715 / 820.2702 = 3.845, which rounds to 3.8, not 3.9. Runs 1 and 2 give 2.620 and 2.690. Correct text: '2.6 to 3.8'.

Wrong number, pass-order bullet (line 207): 'OpenSearch: 6.7 to 7.7 ms'. 1000 divided by the 1-searcher QPS is 1000/150.477 = 6.646 ms (run 3) and 1000/129.841 = 7.702 ms (run 1). The low end rounds to 6.6, not 6.7. Correct text: '6.6 to 7.7 ms'. The Elasticsearch figures in the same bullet (148 to 167/s, 6.0 to 6.8 ms) are correct.

Run mislabelled, Setup 'Runs' bullet (lines 112-113): 'SQL DiskANN joined at run 2. Its third run is a four-target run from 3 Oct 23:48 UTC.' That run (20261003-234838) started before run 2 (4 Oct 13:08), so it is DiskANN's first run in time, not its third. The page's own per-run lists in the SQL section (line 336: 1.5%, 12.2%, 16.4% with 8 searchers; 14.7%, 18.4%, 15.3% with one) are ordered 23:48 run, run 2, run 3, which treats it as first. The label and the list order contradict each other. The six percentages themselves are correct for those pairings.

Misleading because the medians are taken separately (exact-mode table line 314, plus the line 329-330 claim that only DuckDB, ClickHouse and Typesense were slower in exact mode): the SQL DiskANN row shows default 4.50 and exact 4.30, so exact looks faster. Paired by run, exact was slower in 2 of 3 runs: 23:48 run 4.239 default vs 4.305 exact, run 3 4.504 vs 4.772. It was faster only in run 2 (4.565 vs 4.281). Exact was also slower in one run each for MariaDB (run 3: 1.979 vs 2.075), pgvector (run 3: 1.975 vs 3.160) and Oracle (run 2: 4.846 vs 5.626). Every median printed is correct; only the direction the DiskANN row implies is wrong for most runs.

Minor, presentation only: the exact-mode table (lines 309-319) looks sorted by default-search p50 but is not. Qdrant (2.42) sits above Redis (1.51), MariaDB (1.98) and sqlite-vec (2.16), and Oracle (5.56) sits above MongoDB (5.51). The page states no sort order, so this is a hole only if the table is meant to be ranked.

[med] 'At 524 rows, DiskANN bought no measured speed' contradicts the data. DiskANN beat the exact scan in every paired run: qps1 +14.7/+18.4/+15.3%, qps8 +1.5/+12.2/+16.4%, p50 4.24/4.57/4.50 vs 6.18/6.72/6.81 ms. The run-order explanation is tagged 'likely' and not isolated. Say 'no speed gain that survives the order check', not 'no measured speed'.

[med] 'The same query/search, timed later' compares different copies of the data and the page does not say so. SQL: the exact scan inside the DiskANN target runs on database GvbBenchDiskAnn (SqlDiskAnnSink.SearchExactAsync -> _inner, DATABASE='GvbBenchDiskAnn'), while the 'sql' target uses GvbBench. Qdrant: the exact search that was timed later is on collection gvb_..._hnsw, while the 'qdrant' target uses gvb_.... Only sqlite-vec is truly the same table and query. A database or collection effect is not separated from run order.

[med] Durability omission. SqliteVecSink.cs:429-430 sets PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL and synchronous=NORMAL. That is off-default and can lose the latest commits on power loss. It is absent from the sqlite-vec settings row and from the note that says 'Two other settings trade durability' (MariaDB, DuckDB). The DuckDB row also omits checkpoint_threshold 256MB (default 16MB) and memory_limit 8GB (DuckDbSink.cs:496-497).

[low] SQL Server row, 'Server settings off default', lists only PREVIEW_FEATURES. /var/opt/mssql/mssql.conf (dated 2026-09-30, before the runs) sets memory.memorylimitmb=24576 and disables sqlagent. Qdrant's 'none' is confirmed (config.yaml holds only paths and ports).

[low] 'Strong consistency, the client's default' (Milvus) is wrong as worded. Strong is an explicit option of this sink (MilvusSinkOptions.SearchConsistency='Strong', written into every search body). MilvusSink.cs's own doc says Milvus's default is Bounded.

[low] ClickHouse under 'Index choices [measured]': 'bf16 graph without rescoring lost recall' implies bf16/no-rescoring is the cause. Measured: only index path <1.0 (0.985/0.995/0.995) vs exact =1.0. Not isolated; ClickHouseSink.cs's own sweep shows f32 with no rescoring also at 0.995 as loaded.

[low] Lede 'Redis ... 7th with eight' sits beside 'in all three runs' claims. Per run Redis ranked 7th, 7th and 3rd (run 3: 3,154/s, ahead of Qdrant, MongoDB and Elasticsearch). 7th holds only by median. Say 'by median'.
[low] Rounding errors. Redis gain 'to 3.9' should be 3.8 (3154.17/820.27 = 3.845). OpenSearch '6.7 to 7.7 ms' should be 6.6 to 7.7 (1000/150.477 = 6.646).

[low] Untagged causal claims stated as fact: 'On 8 threads, a gain above 8 means a lone search spent part of its time waiting or warming up' (inside the measured-tagged section) and 'Its lone searches were waiting on something' (Milvus). No wait time was measured. CPU frequency or idle states, server-side batching and load differences between passes are not excluded.

[low] 'In-process engines ran one search at a time [measured]': the serialization comes from reading code (DuckDbStore.Gate and SqliteVecStore.Gate held across KnnAsync), not from a number. Measured is only gain <1.0 (DuckDB 0.67-0.78, sqlite-vec 0.87-0.97). A gate alone predicts about 1.0, so the drop below 1.0 is unexplained, and the tag is too strong.

[low] 'No search returned an error' is too broad. SearchRunner.RunAsync discards the result of the 20 warm-up searches (the TimedAsync return is ignored), so warm-up errors are never counted. errors=0 covers only the timed, throughput and exact-mode passes.

[low] Box-load range '1.8 to 8.3' covers only the three table runs. The 3 Oct 23:48 run feeds the SQL paired comparison (6.18 ms p50, +1.5% and +14.7%) and its sql pass started at load 0.13. Range for all data used is 0.13 to 8.25.

[low] Run labelling is inconsistent. 'SQL DiskANN joined at run 2. Its third run is ... 3 Oct 23:48' implies 23:48 is DiskANN's last. Chronologically 23:48 comes before run 2 (13:08) and is DiskANN's first data point. The page elsewhere defines run 2 = 13:08 and run 3 = 13:27.
[trivial] 'Qdrant (256 each), Weaviate (200 each)': 524 splits as 256+256+12 and 200+200+124. Should read 'up to'.

[trivial] 'MariaDB flushed its log once a second, so a crash can lose the last second': with innodb-flush-log-at-trx-commit=2 only an OS crash or power loss loses it, not a mysqld crash. It matches the compose comment but is imprecise.

[source, not page] consolidated.json index text for 'qdrant' says 'HNSW ... built but not used' (TargetFactory.cs; QdrantHnswSink.cs docs also say the graph is built). results.json indexNote in all 4 runs says '0 of 524 vectors in HNSW segments (4 segments)'. The page follows the indexNote (correct) but the stale string contradicts it.

[unverified] 'Index readiness for every engine' names only Milvus and Oracle as not awaited (confirmed: MilvusSink.WaitForIndexAsync and OracleSink.RefreshIndexAsync have no callers). The harness waits for nothing beyond the count for Chroma, Weaviate or Typesense, and whether Chroma indexes asynchronously cannot be checked from the repo.

[unverified externally; repo-only support] DuckDB 'documents as not fully crash safe' (sink doc only). Oracle Free '2 CPU threads' and MariaDB mhnsw_max_cache_size 'default 16M' (compose comments only). DiskANN 'preview, per-database, read-only table, single INT key' (SqlDiskAnnSink doc, author-measured on CU9). Redis/MariaDB/pgvector/Oracle etc. version strings are hard-coded in sinks and pinned by compose image tags; only SQL Server, Qdrant, DuckDB and SQLite are read live. Chroma 1.4.4 confirmed by running the local :latest image.

FOOTER MISMATCH (confirmed, low): footer does not match benchmarks.html. It lacks the foot-about paragraph, the tech-stack span and the Email mailto link, and uses the writeups.html footer pattern (adds Live search, Writeups, Benchmarks links). Head, meta, canonical pattern, inline CSS, topbar, main.doc structure and the theme script match benchmarks.html (script block diff is identical).

SQL ROWS NOT RUN-MATCHED, UNDISCLOSED (confirmed against bench-results/*/results.json): the exact-scan row (806/s, range 765 to 914) is the median of the 18:44, 13:08 and 13:27 runs. It drops the 3 Oct 23:48 run, where exact scored 988/s. The DiskANN row (1,003/s) uses 23:48 + 13:08 + 13:27. So the table gap is +24%, while the paired figures in the page text (+1.5%, +12.2%, +16.4%) are correct and much smaller. MariaDB (4,574/s) and Qdrant exact=false (3,449/s) also had 23:48 results that were left out, with no mention. The page never says the exact scan's 23:48 result was excluded.

RUN CHRONOLOGY WORDING (confirmed): Setup says 'SQL DiskANN joined at run 2. Its third run is a four-target run from 3 Oct 23:48 UTC.' That run predates run 2 (4 Oct 13:08), so it is DiskANN's earliest run, not its third. 'Runs: three' also leaves out that four result files exist.

LEDE RANK BASIS (confirmed, low): 'Redis ... 7th with eight' is the rank by median. Per run Redis was 7th, 7th and 3rd (run 3 at 3,154/s). The page shows the 2,011 to 3,154 range but the lede mixes a per-run claim (pgvector second in all three, which is correct) with a median-rank claim. 'Redis holds everything in memory.' in the caveat card is a mild explain-the-field line (judgment call).

WORKING TREE NOT CLEAN (confirmed, probably pre-existing): git status shows M index.html, model-selection.html, writeups.html and ?? embedder-selection.html, reranker-selection.html in wwwroot, plus M AzdoIndexerService.cs. Their mtimes (1 to 2 Oct) predate vector-engines.html (4 Oct 14:54) and none reference it, so they were not touched by this page. A literal 'no other file modified' check still fails. Related: vector-engines.html has no inbound links, is not in sitemap.xml, and the live URL returns 404 (not deployed). Pushing main would also ship the unrelated dirty files.
